source.authors: Andonov K, Dyugmedzhiev A, Lukanov S, Vacheva E, Popgeorgiev G, Nedeltcheva-Antonova D, Naumov B
source.title: Behavioral effects of long-chained ketones in Vipera ammodytes: an experimental approach

value: adult male nose-horned vipers reacted more strongly to a 1:1 mixture of 2-pentacosanone and 2-heptacosanone than to heptacosane, n-hexane or a blank control paper towel
units: categorical (Bayesian GLMM contrasts judged by the highest posterior density interval: chin-rubbing (positive if rubbing lasted over 10 s) by zero-inflated Poisson; interest (positive if tongue-flicks focused on the towel for at least 10 s) by a binomial model, which the Methods call zero-inflated binomial)
method: terrarium bioassay: paper towel carrying 0.20-0.25 ml of a 1 mg/ml n-hexane solution of 2-pentacosanone (C25), 2-heptacosanone (C27), a mixture of equal parts of both, heptacosane (C27 alkane) or n-hexane alone, or a blank towel (control), kept in the individual's terrarium for 10 min and video-recorded (out-of-sight time subtracted); interest, chin-rubbing, general and specific tongue-flick rates scored; each test repeated three times, compounds presented in random order, no more than four tests per animal per day at least an hour apart, with at least one day between an animal's test days
conditions: wild-sourced: adults caught in April 2022 and April 2023 from one population near Karlukovo, NW Bulgaria, held in captivity no more than two months and released at the capture sites; 15 adults (8 males, 7 females), 270 tests (144 male, 126 female), housed singly in 50 x 30 x 30 cm terraria at 30-32 C by day (09:00-20:00) and about 17 C at night; all tests from early May to the first ten days of June; null and contrary results in the same section: no significant differences among stimuli in males for general or specific tongue-flick rate; in females no significant differences for interest or chin-rubbing for any compound; in females general tongue-flick rate was higher for the mixture than for the C25 ketone and specific tongue-flick rate higher for the C27 ketone than for the alkane and than for the blank control, with the mixture versus the C27 ketone only near-significant; female models had large numbers of zeros and some parts did not converge (R-hat above 1.05) so the authors urge caution; a multivariate GLMM of both sexes found males and females differed in interest and chin-rubbing (males more active toward the compounds), but that model had divergent transitions and R-hat above 1.1; male general tongue-flick rate was highest toward the C25 and C27 ketones but not significantly different from the other compounds; males: the C25 and C27 ketones each differed from the alkane for interest, mixture versus alkane only near-significant; with compounds grouped, males reacted more to ketones than alkanes for interest and chin-rubbing, females had higher specific tongue-flick rate to ketones than to the control; mean latency to first tongue-flick 291 s (n = 128, range 1-593, SD 162.2); the authors call the response to ketones not very pronounced and hypothesise other compounds make up the female sex pheromone; out-of-sight time was subtracted when an individual left the video frame; numeric estimates are in the supplementary material, which the desk did not read
quote: Thus, C25–C27 ketones provoked stronger reactions in males than C27 alkane, hexane, or the control.
note: Classification: behavioural_response, chin-rubbing and interest on a pheromone-candidate ketone mixture against solvent, alkane and blank controls; the value is limited to the contrasts the paper reports and gives no thresholds or effect sizes (numbers sit in the supplement). The quote's 'C25-C27 ketones' is the equal mixture of the two ketones per the Methods.
